long_biography.plain_text:
Shane J. Guidry grew up around the Louisiana marine business founded by his grandfather, Numa Guidry. He joined Harvey Gulf International Marine in 1988, working aboard tugboats before moving through safety, logistics and sales. Guidry became president and chief executive in 1997, taking operational control as the company shifted from inland and offshore towing toward larger vessels serving deepwater energy projects.

The family-company buyout preserved Guidry's equity and managerial control while giving the business institutional capital for expansion. Harvey Gulf sold its towing division, expanded offshore supply and subsea services, and pioneered LNG propulsion and bunkering in the United States. Guidry continues as chairman and chief executive, and a fourth family generation has entered management through his son Ashton, the chief operating officer.
